statement: Each backoffice accepts only its server-fixed account domain and uses a session, cookie, origin, login realm, and cache namespace that cannot be reused by another backoffice.
given: an account and membership assigned to exactly one account domain
when: a principal logs in or calls an authenticated API
an administrator disables a membership, changes a password, or changes role grants
then: the server derives the account domain from the application entry and never from tenantId supplied by the client
credentials, active membership, tenant type, session realm, cookie, origin, and cache namespace must all match that account domain
unknown routes and direct requests without effective permission are denied
old sessions fail after membership disable, password change, revocation, or permission version change
counterexamples: a platform cookie authenticates a merchant or agent request
a login request selects another workspace by supplying tenantId
a cached platform grant authorizes a merchant session
a hidden frontend action succeeds when called directly without its permission
